answer: Require each agent identity to post a locked deposit before it can trade: the stake is slashed if the agent is caught voting twice or copying another's work. A tide of fake identities can still arrive, but each one costs capital, so spinning up ten thousand Sybils means locking ten thousand deposits. Honest agents earn theirs back with fees, like a marble that keeps its value in play, while an attacker must risk forfeiture or park funds that could earn elsewhere. Reputation then works like an opal: it accrues only from completed work under one staked identity, so it cannot be faked overnight.
